name: SAMHI Hotels Ltd
tagline: Branded-hotel platform (~Rs 3,400 Cr, 31 hotels / ~4,900 keys) mid-way through a real operating turnaround - Q1 FY27 RevPAR +9.6%, occupancy 79%, EBITDA margin ~37%, GIC JV validation, EV/EBITDA ~8x FY28E vs peers 11-15x - but still carrying ~3.2x group net debt/EBITDA, deferred-tax-flattered headline earnings, a 0% promoter and a live Rs 750 Cr dilution overhang
business_overview: SAMHI owns and operates 31 hotels (~4,904 keys) across 14 cities under 11 brands (Marriott, Hyatt, IHG affiliations), skewed to business/GCC-corridor markets (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune). The model is 'capital recycling' - acquire distressed/under-managed hotels, re-brand and turn them around, then deleverage. A GIC joint venture holds 35% of three subsidiaries (five hotels), which paid down debt in two of them, and provides the vehicle for upper-scale expansion. New builds underway in Navi Mumbai (~700-key Westin + Fairfield), Whitefield Bengaluru (Westin + Tribute Portfolio, via the JV) and Hyderabad; an early-stage experiential B2C platform (RARE India, 70%) with Marriott, plus a small Itmenaan Lodges acquisition. No promoter - 0% promoter holding, PE/institutionally controlled (FII ~44%, DII ~16%).
fundamentals_table: ROCE ~9% (still below the cost of debt); FY26 ROE optically high on the deferred-tax-inflated PAT
FY24-26 revenue Rs 957 / 1,130 / 1,283 Cr (~16% CAGR); Q1 FY27 comparable +10.8% YoY (reported +7.3% on GST change); management guides 9-11% long-term same-store

EBITDA margin 29.4% -> 36.0% -> 37.3% (FY24-26) on RevPAR-led operating leverage; Q1 FY27 EBITDA +12.1% comparable; GST rate change a near-term headwind; ARR/RevPAR ~Rs 5,220 with a stated path toward Rs 7,500-8,000

CFO ~Rs 357 Cr FY25; net debt ~Rs 1,967 Cr; net debt/EBITDA ~3.2x at group (~2.4x on operating assets); the ~2.4x target is an FY28 goal, not 12-18 months; interest cost falling (Q4 FY26 Rs 37 Cr vs Rs 55 Cr YoY); Rs 750 Cr enabling resolution passed - use unspecified

EV/EBITDA ~10-11x trailing, ~8x FY28E vs Chalet ~15x / Lemon Tree ~13x / Juniper ~11x; headline P/E ~10 flattered by a ~Rs 330 Cr non-cash deferred-tax credit (core multiple ~15-16x); 52-week range Rs 127 - 229
fundamentals_narrative: The operating turnaround is measurable and still running: 3-year revenue CAGR ~16%, EBITDA margin up ~800 bps to 37.3%, Q1 FY27 same-store RevPAR +9.6% and occupancy up to 79.3% from 74.2%, interest cost falling sharply, and GIC's Rs 752 Cr institutional capital validating the asset base (its Rs 2,200 Cr EV mark on three subsidiaries implies the rest of the business is available cheap). Demand tailwind from 1,600+ GCCs concentrated in SAMHI's core cities; domestic guests are now 82% of room-nights, which insulated the June quarter from inbound-travel weakness. The quality caveats are real and this pass sharpened them: leverage is still heavy (net debt ~Rs 1,967 Cr, net debt/EBITDA ~3.2x at group - not 'toward 2.5x'), FY26 headline PAT of Rs 566 Cr is ~2.4x flattered by a non-cash ~Rs 330 Cr deferred-tax-asset creation plus a ~Rs 27 Cr impairment reversal (core PAT ~Rs 230-240 Cr), ROCE (~9%) is below the cost of debt, there is no promoter, and the Rs 750 Cr enabling resolution is a live ~20%-of-mcap dilution overhang with unspecified use. Hotels remain cyclical and the current ~37% EBITDA margin is likely toward a cyclical peak.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Fell ~30-35% into early 2026 on Middle East / travel-cost fears from an already-cheap level; members frame the drawdown as fear-driven rather than fundamental. Price ~Rs 153 as of early Sep 2026, near the lower half of the 52-week range.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent ~20 of 401 posts (Feb 2026 to Aug 2026). Constructive but patient. Aloysius_De_Sa (elevated): 'Blessing for long-term investors. Management has been walking the talk and the market is giving opportunities to add... pre-war this stock was trading way cheaper than what I believed was fair value. Not concerned at all.' Markmaker, bijo_scaria ('my bet on SAMHI is the next 5 years - Mumbai/Bengaluru/Hyderabad projects + higher EBITDA + strong cash generation + deleveraging'), Aiyappaa and k3311 are all invested and positive, citing the peer-valuation gap and the GCC/ARR runway. Rishabh_Modi is the balanced sceptic - 'cheap, but there is a reason': ROCE < interest rate, and the GIC deal is a complex equity dilution (~Rs 752 Cr non-controlling interest). On the Rs 750 Cr raise, aditya14920251 and bijo_scaria caution that management has NOT said it is for debt paydown - it is a strategic/contingency option, possibly for distressed-asset acquisition.
community_signal: A genuine positive conviction signal from an elevated member (Aloysius_De_Sa) - 'management walking the talk', adding on weakness, 'not concerned at all'. Supported by several invested (non-trusted) members with a multi-year thesis. The counter-view (Rishabh_Modi) is about quality/returns, not a governance concern.
bse_notes: GIC JV: 35% stake in three subsidiaries (five hotels), Rs 752 Cr (Rs 603 Cr upfront primarily to cut debt + Rs 149 Cr for Whitefield Westin/Tribute capex); Rs 2,200 Cr EV; ~Rs 752 Cr non-controlling interest now on the balance sheet. Rs 750 Cr capital-raise enabling resolution passed Q1 FY27 - purpose not specified (optionality/contingency, possibly distressed-asset acquisition). Mar 2026: acquired 70% of RARE India (experiential B2C, with Marriott) and Itmenaan Lodges. Navi Mumbai ~700-key dual-branded Westin + Fairfield - MIDC approved a project extension. Q4 FY26 PAT boosted by a ~Rs 330 Cr deferred-tax-asset creation and a ~Rs 27 Cr impairment reversal (non-cash). No SEBI action; no red-flag tier.

value_chain.theme: India branded-hotel upcycle / GCC-corridor corporate demand

value_chain.note: Three years of strong RevPAR are pulling new supply back into SAMHI's core markets - a late-upcycle position. SAMHI's edge is buying distressed assets below replacement cost and re-branding, not pricing power.

one-off ~Rs 330 Cr deferred-tax credit flattering FY26 PAT (non-recurring)
earnings_quality.normalised_note: 37.3% EBITDA margin is toward a cyclical peak for an asset-heavy owner after three up years; a through-cycle level is likely mid-30s. FY26 PAT of Rs 566 Cr normalises to ~Rs 230-240 Cr ex the ~Rs 330 Cr deferred-tax credit.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: RevPAR YoY oldest->newest: ~17% (FY25) -> ~10% (FY26) -> +9.6% (Q1 FY27); comparable revenue YoY ~16% (FY25) -> ~13% (FY26) -> +10.8% (Q1 FY27). Growth has settled into the guided 9-11% band and is holding, with occupancy (+5pp YoY in Q1) and margin still improving.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: Growth has normalised to the guided 9-11%; the ~10-11x trailing EV/EBITDA already reflects a steady mid-cycle grower, so the re-rating case rests on deleveraging + new builds, not on an acceleration.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Capital-recycling model executed reasonably - bought distressed hotels below replacement cost, lifted asset EBITDA ~21% in FY25; incremental returns still modest (group ROCE ~9%, below the cost of debt); the GIC JV brought institutional capital at a Rs 2,200 Cr EV mark. RARE India (70%) and Itmenaan are small adjacent bets, mildly diversifying.
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Moving from economy/mid-scale turnarounds up to upper-scale/premium via the GIC JV (Westin, Tribute Portfolio) and experiential travel (RARE + Marriott)

four_box.note: tam and moat weak - capital-intensive cyclical on licensed third-party brands, ROCE below the cost of debt, headroom for a 2-4x rather than a comfortable 10x; tailwind (structural GCC demand) + a genuine valuation discount (~8x FY28E vs peers 11-15x, near book) carry it to 3.0, so the 10x label is permitted but the realistic case is a 2-4x.

track_record.note: Screener FY20-FY26: ROCE never above 9% (range -8% to 9%); rev growth cleared >=10% in most years but ROCE >=15% in none - 0 of 7. FY26 PAT Rs567cr is inflated by a ~Rs300cr deferred-tax credit (tax rate -112%), so FY26 ROE ~24% is not representative.

quality_metrics.note: Acquisition-led branded-hotel owner (Marriott/IHG/Hyatt). ROCE -4%->7%->9%->9% FY21-25 - improving as occupancy/ARR recover, still below cost of capital; FY26 ROCE not displayed (headline ROE 24% is deferred-tax-inflated). OPM 28%->36%->35%. Borrowings de-levered Rs2,744cr->Rs1,854cr but still ~4.2x EBITDA. Trailing-3y FCF conversion ~+48% (CFO Rs1,039cr vs capex Rs509cr FY24-26) - genuinely cash-generative now; a further Rs750cr raise was approved Aug-2026.
